title: Managing & Altering Views
description: Modify views safely, handle dependencies, and drop views with CASCADE / RESTRICT.

data.text: When managing views, `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` allows updating the view query, provided the existing projected columns remain identical in order and data type. If column types change or columns are removed, you must drop and recreate the view.

data.title: Altering and Dropping Views
data.content: Dropping with cascade to clean up dependencies.

data.text: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` is safe only when the existing columns keep the same names, order, and types: you may append new columns, but not rename or retype existing ones. When a change does violate that rule, the reliable path is to drop and recreate the view inside a transaction, then rebuild dependent views in the correct order.

data.title: Append a column, then find dependents
data.content: Appending a column is a valid replace. To see what depends on a view before dropping it, query the catalog.
data.code:
-- Allowed: append a column at the end
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_order_summary AS
SELECT
    o.id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.amount,
    o.status,
    o.ordered_at
FROM orders AS o;

-- What depends on this view?
SELECT DISTINCT
    dependent.relname AS dependent_object
FROM pg_depend d
JOIN pg_rewrite r   ON r.oid = d.objid
JOIN pg_class   src ON src.oid = d.refobjid
JOIN pg_class   dependent ON dependent.oid = r.ev_class
WHERE src.relname = 'v_order_summary'
  AND dependent.relname <> 'v_order_summary';

data.title: CASCADE is a loaded gun
data.text: `DROP VIEW ... CASCADE` silently removes everything that depends on the view, including other views and, in older setups, rules. In production, prefer dropping and recreating the full dependency chain inside a single transaction so a failure rolls everything back rather than leaving a half-dropped schema.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot rename existing columns or alter column types.
Use `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS ... CASCADE` if other dependent views exist.
Track view definitions in version-controlled migration files.
